title: Add graceful throttle memory probe and rollback sentry
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a memory-aware graceful throttle probe and an adaptive rollback sentry for canary evaluations. Improves resilience against memory-induced latency spikes by scoring rollback risk and pausing traffic ramps when memory pressure correlates with tail latency degradation.
description: Context: We continue to see short-lived latency regressions that correlate strongly with transient GPU/host memory pressure during warmup and during certain batched workloads. Existing canary detectors focused on latency/throughput signals can overreact (false positives) or underreact (missed degradations) when memory pressure is the root cause. This PR introduces two complementary components: 1) a lightweight Memory Probe that samples per-host GPU/OS memory utilization distributions and computes short-window entropy and tail co-moments with latency; 2) a Rollback Sentry that fuses the memory signal with existing canary scorecards to produce a risk score used by the rollout controller to throttle or stop canary ramps. Design summary: - Memory Probe: continuous sampling (1s aggregated) of resident GPU memory, allocator fragmentation metric, and RSS for the inference process. Computes 95/99 percentiles, short-window skew, and an entropy-like measure that detects unexpected dispersion in memory usage across hosts. - Correlation layer: streaming correlation (Spearman, robust to outliers) between memory 95/99 percentiles and tail latency (p95/p99). Correlations maintained as exponentially weighted moving estimates to react quickly but avoid single-spike sensitivity. - Rollback Sentry: takes inputs from the canary evaluator (latency deltas, throughput deltas, error rates) and memory-correlation outputs to compute a single 0-100 risk score. Rules: if risk >= 70 -> immediate canary pause and automatic rollback candidate; if risk in 50-70 -> throttle ramp and require manual ACK; risk < 50 -> normal rollout. The sentry also factors in traffic-weighted amplification to reduce noisy signals from low-volume slices. Motivation: By adding memory-awareness we reduce both false-positive rollbacks triggered by transient GC/allocator events and false-negatives where latency regressions are caused by memory saturation rather than model-level regressions. Checklist: - [x] Memory Probe implementation and unit tests - [x] Streaming correlation module and integration tests - [x] Rollout Sentry scoring logic and policy configuration - [x] E2E synthetic workload tests (bursty batch, warmup scenarios) - [x] Dashboard panels and alerts for memory-correlation heatmap - [x] Documentation and operator runbook - [x] Canary experiment in perf-canary staging cluster Testing and validation: Ran staged canary on perf-canary/staging across three workload shapes (steady small-batch, bursty batch, mixed latency-sensitive). Observed a 38% reduction in unnecessary rollback events in synthetic warmup tests and correct blocking of a memory-induced p99 regression in one injected fault run. CI: unit and integration suites passed, one flaky host-level metric test stabilized by increasing aggregation window. Rollout plan: - Roll out to canary evaluator in staging for 48 hours - Gradual opt-in for new canaries (default off for legacy rollout jobs) - Monitor heatmap and false-positive rate for two weeks before defaulting to on. Configuration: all thresholds and weights are feature-flagged and tunable via canary policy YAML. Operator note: if your environment has external memory reclamation hooks (custom allocators) set memory_probe.skip_low_level=true to avoid noisy fragmentation signals.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice approach. Can you justify the 70/50 thresholds? How sensitive are they across clusters?
Maya Chen: Thresholds are conservative and feature-flagged. We derived them from 120 synthetic runs across 6 host types; added a config map so SREs can tune per-region.
Priya Rao: Please add a safety valve that ignores memory signals for very low traffic slices to avoid overfitting to noise.
Maya Chen: Added traffic-weighted amplification and a skip_low_volume flag; updated tests to cover that case.
Diego Martinez: CI flake in integration test — looks like metric ingestion race. Recommend increasing aggregation window to 1s for the sampler.
Maya Chen: Increased aggregation window and added retry logic; re-ran CI and green.
